execution: Reasoning-only static review. Fable executed no tools, tests, builds or measurements. Correctness/performance evidence was generated by Codex and provided in the prompt.

review.review_basis: Static reasoning only by claude-fable-5-2. No tools were run, no edits made, no tests executed. The SHA256 of the frozen source and all Codex evidence and measurements are taken as reported, not verified by me.

correctness_findings.detail: Every write to parent/base/outer inside augment hits a vertex in cursor[0..reached). The root is cursor[0]. An inner vertex vi is appended in the same statement group as parent[vi]=u, before the free-vertex check, so it is recorded on the success path too. Its mate is appended immediately before outer[mate]=1. mark() writes parent only for vertices on the tree paths from u and v to the common base, all of which are outer and therefore already listed. The contraction loop writes base/outer only for i taken from the list. The path flip touches partners_ only.

vi is appended only when outer[vi]==0 and parent[vi]==-1, which excludes the root, every earlier inner vertex and every earlier mate. Its mate cannot already be listed: if it were an inner vertex, vi would be outer; if it had been appended as a mate, parent[vi] would not be -1; and it is not the root because the root is unmatched. So the entries are distinct, reached <= N, the highest index written by cursor[reached++] is N-1, and the search can never overwrite cursor[N].

The workspace constructor value-initializes cursor(n+1), so cursor[N]==0. CSR construction writes only cursor[i] for i<n and cursor[u], cursor[v] for vertex indices below n. The first augment therefore sees 0 and takes the full fill/iota/fill path, which is required because parent and base are zero-initialized rather than -1/identity, and the CSR leftovers in cursor[0..N) are never read as vertices. Every augment sets reached>=1 and stores it on both exits, so 0 uniquely identifies the first search of a workspace.

By induction, after either reset path the state equals parent=-1, base=identity, outer=0. The full path does this unconditionally. The sparse path restores exactly the vertices the previous search dirtied, and by the coverage finding nothing else was dirtied. The previous list is fully consumed before cursor[0]=root overwrites it. A big search followed by a small one, or the reverse, is safe because each search writes a complete list and count regardless of which reset preceded it. For N<4, N/4==0, so the full path is always taken. Since the post-reset state is identical to the baseline's, search order and the resulting matching are identical to the baseline, not merely another maximum matching.

ancestor/contracted and the reset-on-wrap in join are untouched. They never needed per-search clearing: generation is strictly fresh per join, and a wrap zero-fills both arrays before restarting at 1. An unreached vertex i cannot have contracted[base[i]]==generation, because stamps of the current generation are placed only on bases of tree vertices.

With n==0, solve returns at the maximum_ check or at cardinality_==n/2 before any workspace exists, so augment is unreachable; cursor would have size 1 in any case. n+1 cannot overflow (n comes from int32, and the SIZE_MAX guard remains). The guard m<=max_size/2 keeps m*2 safe. The always-on protections stated in the header are intact.

No issues found. verify_in has static storage, so its buffer is zero-initialized before first use. The sentinel digit loop refills only when position_==size_. The integer writer reserves 22 bytes, enough for any 64-bit value. The output object flushes in its destructor at exit. Under SKIP_RUNTIME_CHECKS, well-formed input is a documented precondition, as before.

API_ownership_findings.detail: No public signature, view lifetime or complexity statement changes. The workspace is still a solve-local automatic object with the same nine vector allocations, plus one size_t of payload in cursor.

Exception guarantees are unchanged. All allocations finish in the workspace constructor before partners_ or cardinality_ are modified. augment remains noexcept and contains only indexing and trivial writes. The claim that solve changes the matching only after all workspace is allocated still holds. Copy, move, swap and reset are untouched.
The count lives in the workspace, not in GeneralMatching, so it cannot go stale across solve calls, clear_matching, add_edge or copies. Each solve starts from cursor[N]==0.

performance_assessment.summary: Keep. Initialization per search drops from O(N) to O(previous reached) when the previous search was small, and the N/4 fallback preserves the vectorized sequential fills when most of the graph was touched.
performance_assessment.why_the_numbers_are_plausible: The reported profile matches the mechanism: large gains where there are many tiny searches (disjoint triangles, sparse cases) and parity on dense inputs, where the sparse path would mean about three random writes per vertex against streaming fills.
performance_assessment.added_cost: One load and one well-predicted branch per augment, and one store per exit.
performance_assessment.online_time: The full program is IO-dominated and measured flat (+0.06%, noise). Not claiming an online improvement is the right call, and the 2ms AC applies only to the previously uploaded source.
performance_assessment.rejected_alternatives: Rejecting the packed allocation and make_unique_for_overwrite variants on a 6-8% dense regression, and keeping the adaptive fallback over always-sparse, is consistent with the reasoning above.
performance_assessment.caveat: The early Clang flower500 ratio of 1.507 was explained by the longer recheck (1.0086), which I accept as noise but cannot confirm.

unmeasured_suggestion.label: UNMEASURED
unmeasured_suggestion.idea: After a failed search, permanently retire the vertices in its reached list. A Hungarian forest from a failed root can never lie on a later augmenting path, so later searches could skip those vertices, shrinking both the search and the reset on inputs with many failing roots.
unmeasured_suggestion.risk: This is an algorithmic change, not an initialization tweak. It needs a separate dead flag, because leaving outer/parent stale would corrupt join, and it needs its own proof and differential testing. Do not fold it into this frozen round.

optional_suggestion_disposition: Not adopted: UNMEASURED algorithmic proposal is outside this frozen initialization change; no correctness/performance endorsement of that proposal.
